name: Sable Okonkwo-Reinholt
description: Sable Okonkwo-Reinholt rose from a Tier 2 fabrication district in the old Milwaukee Annex by broadcasting her unfiltered emotional states during a 72-hour labor strike in 2211 — her raw grief and solidarity feeding directly into 4 million neural subscribers. She streams what she calls 'living grief,' emotional landscapes tied to her work as a trauma counselor in Shelf clinics, and her feed is known for the physical sensation of crying without knowing why. Her signature is a voluntary BCI vulnerability she calls 'the open window,' which strips all emotional filtering from her broadcasts.
cultural_impact: Sable normalized emotional labor as a public act, and her strike broadcast is credited with shifting public sympathy during the 2211 Fabricator Walkout. Her 'open window' technique has been replicated by thousands of amateur feeders, creating a subculture of unfiltered emotional broadcasting.
key_figures: Dr. Yemi Strausberg (the neuroscientist who certified her open-window protocol)
locations: The Underbowl Arena (where she hosts live feed events)
story_hooks: Sable's open-window broadcast picks up something she didn't intend — a memory that isn't hers, leaking in from an unknown source — and 4 million people experience it simultaneously before she can cut the feed.
A corponation offers Sable an enormous contract to broadcast 'managed grief' for a product launch memorial event, and she's considering it because her Shelf clinic is about to lose funding.
Someone is systematically targeting open-window broadcasters with a signal that turns their emotional feeds into weapons — inducing panic in subscribers — and Sable is next on the list.
controversy: In 2213, a subscriber sued her after experiencing a dissociative episode during an open-window broadcast, claiming her feed overwrote three days of their own emotional memory. The case was settled out of court but sparked ongoing legislation around unfiltered BCI broadcasting.
